title: Live browser • public API documentation
caption: Fresh browser interactions, not a slideshow. Synthetic data only; this public demo uses unencrypted HTTP.

title: Live API • health check
caption: Use Swagger Try it out and Execute. This sends a real request to the existing GKE application.

title: Live API • valid synthetic transaction
caption: Paste five explicit strings. The API validates a request; it does not transfer money or store balances.

title: Live API • Zero amount
caption: Change only the amount to zero. This is a business-rule rejection: HTTP 200, valid false, AMOUNT_NOT_POSITIVE.

title: Live API • Same sender and recipient
caption: Use the same opaque account identifier twice. The business rule rejects a self-transfer request.

title: Live API • Excess fractional precision
caption: Use three fractional digits. The service rejects excess precision rather than silently rounding money.

title: Live API • Wrong input type
caption: Send a JSON number instead of a decimal string. Strict boundary validation returns HTTP 422 without echoing the submitted value.

title: Live API • Unknown request field
caption: Add an undocumented field. Extra request fields are rejected; the public contract is not silently expanded.

title: Live API • Restore a valid request
caption: Remove the extra field and restore the documented payload. The same running endpoint accepts the valid request again.

title: Reviewed source • exact API contract
caption: Read the published contract: schema failures and business rejections are different. Identifiers are case-sensitive; money uses Decimal.

title: Reviewed source • pure business rules
caption: HTTP handling and Pydantic schemas are separate from transaction rules. The service performs no network or filesystem I/O.

title: Reviewed source • container build and runtime
caption: The Dockerfile builds a locked package and defines a non-root runtime. This source review does not rebuild or execute a vulnerable artifact.

title: Reviewed source • CI gate ordering
caption: The Jenkinsfile places tests and security checks before image release. Actual retained Jenkins results follow; no job is triggered for this recording.
